limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on the barrel cortex of the mouse somatosensory system; findings may not generalize to other cortical areas or species.
The impairment in synapse maturation is transient and resolves by adulthood (P27-P33).
The exact molecular mechanisms by which microglia influence glutamate receptor maturation remain speculative (e.g., phagocytosis, cytokine release).
Only a subset of synaptic properties (AMPAR/NMDAR ratio, NMDAR subunit composition, paired-pulse ratio) were examined; other forms of plasticity were not tested.
The study does not directly demonstrate that microglial entry into barrel centers causes the synaptic maturation; it shows correlation and genetic evidence.

methods.name: Immunohistochemistry and confocal imaging
methods.protocol_description: Urethane-anesthetized mice perfused with 4% PFA. 50-μm tangential or coronal sections. Primary antibodies: anti-5-HTT (1:1000), anti-VGluT2 (1:1000), anti-Iba1 (1:1000), anti-CX3CL1 (1:50). Secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 546, Alexa Fluor 633, Cy3. TO-PRO-3 nuclear stain. Confocal images spanning 30 ± 6 μm.

methods.name: Quantitative analysis of microglial distribution
methods.protocol_description: ImageJ used to count microglial cells inside and outside TCA clusters in tangential sections. Barrel periphery defined by borders of neighboring TCA clusters. Six barrels of rows B and C per animal. Data presented as mean ± SEM. One-way ANOVA followed by Mann-Whitney U test.

experiments_or_tasks: Minimal stimulation of TCAs to evoke EPSCs; measurement of AMPAR/NMDAR ratio, paired-pulse ratio, NMDAR decay kinetics, and sensitivity to GluN2B antagonist Ro256981.
Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings from layer 4 neurons in thalamocortical acute slices of barrel cortex at P5-P10 and P27-P33.

methods.name: Thalamocortical slice preparation and electrophysiology
methods.protocol_description: TC slices (400 μm) from P5-P33 mice prepared in ice-cold sucrose solution (in mM: 215 sucrose, 2.5 KCl, 1.25 NaH2PO4, 26 NaHCO3, 20 glucose, 5 pyruvate, 1 CaCl2, 7 MgCl2, bubbled with carbogene, pH 7.4, 310 mOsm). Slices incubated 30-45 min at 33°C, then maintained at RT in NaCl-based solution (126 mM NaCl, 1 mM MgCl2, 2 mM CaCl2). Whole-cell recordings from layer 4 neurons with CsMeSO3-based intracellular solution. Minimal stimulation protocol (0.2 ms, 0.05 Hz) with bipolar electrode in internal capsule. AMPAR and NMDAR EPSCs measured at -70 mV and +40 mV. EPSC decays fitted with double exponential; weighted time constant calculated. Paired-pulse ratio at -70 mV with 60 ms interval. Ro256981 (300 nM) applied to assess GluN2B contribution. Drugs: NBQX, D-AP-5, gabazine.

study_units.name: Electrophysiological analysis of thalamocortical synapses in CX3CR1-deficient mice

provenance.text_excerpt: the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio gradually increased in CX3CR1 +/eGFP mice of P5 (N = 5, the number of cells n is given in Fig. 2G), P7 (N = 10) and P9 (N = 17; Fig. 2F). At this latter stage, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio of CX3CR1 +/eGFP mice (0.75 ± 0.09) was not significantly different from that of CX3CR1 +/+ mice (0.84 ± 0.12; n = 9, 3 animals). In contrast, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio at thalamocortical synapses of CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP mice did not change significantly over the same developmental window (Fig. 2F) with mean values remaining below 0.5 at P5 (N = 3), P7 (N = 5), and P9 (N = 6; Fig. 2G). Consequently, the AMPAR/NMDAR ratio at P9 was significantly lower in CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP than in CX3CR1 +/eGFP mice (Fig. 2G).

results.value_raw_text: In CX3CR1+/eGFP mice, AMPAR/NMDAR ratio increased from P5 to P9 (P9: 0.75 ± 0.09). In CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice, ratio remained below 0.5 at P5, P7, P9; significantly lower at P9 compared to CX3CR1+/eGFP.

results.value_raw_text: Paired-pulse depression did not differ between CX3CR1+/eGFP and CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP mice at P5, P7, P9.

provenance.text_excerpt: The charge of NMDAR-mediated responses was reduced by 21.48 ± 5.38% (N = 7) and by 44.32 ± 5.60% (N = 5) in CX3CR1 +/eGFP and in CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP mice, respectively (Fig. 3A,B), indicating that a higher proportion of GluN2B-containing NMDARs were maintained at maturating synapses of CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP.

results.value_raw_text: Ro256981 reduced NMDAR charge by 21.48 ± 5.38% in CX3CR1+/eGFP (N=7) and 44.32 ± 5.60% in CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP (N=5) at P9-P10.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: the decay time constant of NMDAR-mediated synaptic currents in P27–P33 animals did not differ between CX3CR1 +/eGFP (N = 8) and CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP (N = 4) mice (Fig. 3D) and was similar to that of CX3CR1 +/+ animals (107.71 ± 8.23 ms; n = 12; N = 8; p ≥ 0.5, unpaired t test with Welch correction).

provenance.text_excerpt: the weighted decay time constant of NMDAR-mediated synaptic currents at thalamocortical synapses of CX3CR1 +/eGFP mice decreased from 187.79 ± 6.29 ms at P5–P7 (N = 7) to 145.42 ± 12.07 ms at P9–P10 (N = 11; Fig. 3C,D). In contrast, in CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP mice this decay time constant did not change between P5 and P7 (198.69 ± 22.15 ms; N = 6) and P9 and P10 (197.06 ± 15.07 ms; N = 10; p = 0.95; Fig. 3C,D). Consequently, the decay time constant of NMDAR-mediated synaptic responses at P9–P10 was slower in CX3CR1 eGFP/eGFP mice than in CX3CR1 +/eGFP mice (Fig. 3D).

results.value_raw_text: In CX3CR1+/eGFP, decay τ decreased from 187.79 ± 6.29 ms (P5-P7, N=7) to 145.42 ± 12.07 ms (P9-P10, N=11). In CX3CR1eGFP/eGFP, no change: 198.69 ± 22.15 ms (P5-P7, N=6) vs 197.06 ± 15.07 ms (P9-P10, N=10); significantly slower at P9-P10 than CX3CR1+/eGFP. Adult (P27-P33) decay τ similar between genotypes.
